title: Coordinate Hilbert polynomial and canonical geometric-fibre embeddings
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq0$, and $i:X\to\mathbf P^n_k$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where projective space is the standard base-change construction [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Put $S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and let $S_d$ be its vector subspace of polynomials homogeneous of total degree $d\in\mathbf N$. On each standard chart $U_a=D_+(x_a)$ identify the dehomogenization $F/x_a^d$ with its polynomial section. Define $I_d(i)$ to be the $k$-linear span of those $F\in S_d$ whose dehomogenization restricts to zero on $i^{-1}U_a$ for every $a=0,\ldots,n$. Define the coordinate piece $C_d(i)=S_d/I_d(i)$ and coordinate dimension $h_i(d)=\dim_k C_d(i)$. The coordinate Hilbert polynomial predicate on $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ is $\operatorname{IsCoordinatePolynomial}(i,P)\iff\exists N\in\mathbf N,\ \forall d\geq N,\ P(d)=h_i(d)$. This defines a predicate and does not assert existence of such a polynomial. For arbitrary schemes $T,Z,T'$, $i:Z\to\mathbf P^n_T$ and $g:T'\to T$, writing $p:\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ for the projection, define $i_g:Z\times_TT'\to\mathbf P^n_{T'}$ as the canonical morphism induced by the two projections of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], namely by $Z\times_TT'\to Z\xrightarrow{i}\mathbf P^n_T$ and $Z\times_TT'\to T'$. For $t\in T$, define $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}\to T$ as the composite induced by the inclusion of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] in its chosen algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $i_{\bar t}$ is the specified embedding of the geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] whenever $i$ is an embedding.
